tests_added: pipeline/test_hcris_import.py (12 tests: state-prefix filtering, fiscal-year derivation from fy_end_dt not the download bucket, deterministic dedup tie-break, and the invalid-format failure path)
stories.notes: Real data: 256 OK/TX rural/CAH hospitals, 260 cost-report-years, live in Supabase, verified idempotent (identical content hash across two runs from a clean state). Every worksheet/line/column code cited against the CMS data dictionary and confirmed against a real downloaded report before being trusted. Two real bugs found by checking my own output rather than trusting the first run: a DuckDB lazy-evaluation bug (fixed by materializing pivots into real temp tables instead of reusing a shared view name) and a fiscal-year mislabeling bug (CMS's FY2024 download bucket is when CMS processed a report, not each report's own period end -- fixed by deriving fiscal_year from fy_end_dt). Only FY2024 has been run so far; STORY-002 (early-warning flags) and expanding to 3 years remain.

stories.notes: Criteria 2 and 3 were already genuinely true in the repo, built while hardening STORY-001: cost_report_years.operating_margin_pct/days_cash_on_hand/days_in_ar (REQ-002) are Postgres GENERATED ALWAYS AS STORED columns, so they can never drift from source_rpt_rec_num/source_file/metric_provenance. metric_provenance is a per-metric jsonb {wksht_cd, line_num, clmn_num, status} recording exactly which worksheet/line/column each value came from and whether it was ok/not_reported/unparseable -- live-backfilled across all 652 existing rows, 18 confirmed genuinely not_reported. Criterion 1 is left false on purpose: it asks for 'monthly metrics', but CMS HCRIS cost reports carry one annual figure per hospital fiscal year -- there is no month in this data source to slice. REQ-002 (the requirement this story fulfills) correctly says 'per hospital per year'; 'monthly metrics' is REQ-011/STORY-011's language (operator-uploaded monthly exports, release r2), and appears to have been copied into this story's acceptance criteria by mistake. tests_added: frontend/src/lib/hospitalSearch.test.ts (5 tests: name-search happy path, not-found returns an empty list rather than an error, and a data-retrieval error is surfaced as a typed result instead of thrown)

frontend/src/lib/hospitalDetail.test.ts (7 tests: three-years-ascending happy path, fewer-than-three-years without fabricating the gap, hospital-not-found short-circuits before querying years, data-retrieval errors from both the hospital and years lookups, and formatMetric never renders a missing value as zero or blank)
stories.notes: No Supabase client credentials (project URL + anon key) existed locally at the start of this story -- only DATABASE_URL, a direct Postgres connection string used by the Python pipeline. Considered querying Postgres directly from Next.js with that string instead of requesting a new credential, but rejected it: Vercel serverless functions are ephemeral and would exhaust Supabase's direct-connection limit under real traffic, which is exactly why Supabase fronts Postgres with a pooler and recommends the REST API / supabase-js for serverless clients. Got the anon/publishable key from the user instead (frontend/.env.local, gitignored) and built on supabase-js, which also matches this story's own task_guidance ('Next.js frontend ... with data from Supabase'). Search is case-insensitive partial-name match (ilike), not exact match, since public users won't know a hospital's exact CMS-registered name string -- a stricter reading of 'a hospital name' was considered and rejected as needlessly hostile to the actual user. Verified against live production data, not just mocks: a hospital with all three fiscal years (ST ANTHONY SHAWNEE HOSPITAL, CCN 370149) renders 2023/2024/2025 in order, and a hospital with a genuine gap (ANSON GENERAL HOSPITAL, CCN 670781, missing FY2023) renders only its real 2 years plus an explicit 'reporting gap, not an error' note rather than a fabricated third row. The 'notes public data lag' criterion is a static, honest disclosure about CMS's filing-and-processing delay, not a computed lag figure -- there is no per-row lag data in the source to compute one from, and inventing a number would violate the project's own grounding guardrail (REQ-004).

tests_added: pipeline/test_early_warning.py (10 tests: each of the 3 criteria genuinely triggering, a fully healthy hospital with real falling-AR data correctly not flagged, missing metrics marked not_assessable rather than silently cleared, a real trigger winning over an unrelated missing metric, fewer-than-3-years and a real non-consecutive reporting gap both correctly not_assessable for the AR-trend criterion, and a falling AR trend correctly not_triggered rather than not_assessable)
stories.notes: Missing data is never treated as 'no problem': a criterion whose required metric is null is 'not_assessable', not 'not_triggered', and a hospital is only reported 'not_flagged' overall if every criterion was actually checked -- an early-warning system that quietly clears a hospital it couldn't check would defeat its own purpose. Precedence is flagged > not_assessable > not_flagged, so a real trigger is never hidden behind an unrelated missing metric (verified live: CCN 123456-style case with a real trigger + a missing metric elsewhere still flags). 'Days in A/R rising two years in a row' requires three CONSECUTIVE fiscal years, not just the latest three rows on file -- a hospital with a real reporting gap (missing fiscal year, an already-known pattern in this dataset) is correctly not_assessable for this one criterion rather than comparing non-adjacent years as if they were adjacent, which would silently understate what 'two years in a row' actually means. Flags are stored as one current-state row per hospital (early_warning_flags, PK provider_ccn), replaced on each run via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, not appended as history -- re-running the evaluator is idempotent (verified live: ran twice against production, 274 rows before and after, no duplicates, identical distribution). Ran for real against all 274 hospitals in production Supabase: 257 flagged, 16 not assessable, 1 genuinely healthy (RICE MEDICAL CENTER, CCN 451312 -- 5.84% margin, 55.8 days cash, falling A/R). The high flag rate is a real finding about this population (rural/Critical Access hospitals nationally run on thin or negative margins), not a logic bug -- spot-checked individual hospitals' exact stored values against the flag verdict to confirm. Public read RLS on the new table, same as hospitals/cost_report_years: no management-company scoping exists yet since STORY-006 (row-level security) and STORY-005 (operator uploads, the thing that would actually need company-level scoping) aren't built. Reused the exact 'latest 3 fiscal years, ascending' query shape from frontend/src/lib/hospitalDetail.ts so the flag evaluator and the public Health Snapshot page can never disagree about which years count as 'the latest three'.

tests_added: pipeline/test_phi_guardrail.py (22 tests: header-based detection for all three REQ-009 categories -- patient names, birth dates, record numbers; an SSN-shaped-content fallback for a mislabeled column; false-positive avoidance on ordinary business dates; and the ingest gate proving rejection happens before storage and before the PHI value itself ever reaches the audit log)
stories.notes: REQ-009's own wording ('reject... before it is stored or logged') requires real gating behavior, not just a detector -- STORY-011's grounding_guardrail.py was built the same standalone way and stayed unticked until something actually calls it, so scan_file_for_phi() alone would not have earned these criteria. Added ingest_file_with_phi_gate(file_name, rows, store=, log_audit=): store is only called when the scan is clean, never for a rejected file (proven by test_gate_rejects_a_file_with_patient_names_before_storage / test_gate_rejects_a_file_with_birth_dates_before_storage asserting store was never called), and log_audit always receives a PhiAuditEntry naming the column and category that triggered rejection but never the row content itself (test_gate_audit_log_never_contains_the_raw_row_content, test_gate_birth_date_value_never_reaches_the_audit_log). store/log_audit are injected because the real Supabase write and logger do not exist yet (STORY-005, not started) -- STORY-005 plugs in the real implementations without changing this function. Two-layer detection: column-header match for all three categories (deterministic, matches how a real hospital-system export would label these fields) plus an SSN-content fallback for a column mislabeled with an innocuous header. Deliberately not attempted: generic content-based matching for names or dates by shape alone -- financial exports carry legitimate business dates (report date, posting date) and free text cannot reliably be classified as 'a name' without a model, so that would trade false rejections of clean ledger data for coverage the header check already provides in the realistic case; documented as a known limitation in the module docstring, not left silent.

tests_added: pipeline/test_export_normalizer.py (14 tests: two different vendor formats reconciling to the same standard metric names/values, unknown format correctly marked needs_mapping (including a fingerprint missing just one column), totals rows dropped without corrupting source_row provenance for the rows that follow, a malformed month producing a failed outcome rather than a crash, a missing per-row column producing failed rather than a crash, denial rate left None rather than a fake 0% when there are zero total claims, file-hash determinism for the idempotency key, CSV round-tripping, and the PHI audit log line being valid JSON that never carries the flagged cell value)
stories.notes: Built under .colaberry's STORY-011 definition (Convert Hospital System Exports to Standard Metrics, REQ-011, release r1) after finding this is a third instance of the .colaberry/.hospulse numbering collision already documented for STORY-010 and STORY-003: .hospulse's own STORY-011 is an unrelated cost-report-co-pilot story (REQ-015, release r4), and its own REQ-011 equivalent is fulfilled by .hospulse's STORY-008 instead, which is also not started. Followed the same precedent as before -- build .colaberry's definition, leave docs/stories/STORY-011.md un-rewritten since it reflects .hospulse's numbering repo-wide, not just this one file. No operator-upload path exists yet (STORY-005, not started), so 'an export from a hospital system' is raw file bytes handed directly to export_normalizer.run() -- the upload UI is out of this story's scope. Two illustrative vendor mappings (Epic, Cerner) prove the mechanism: mappings.detect_format() matches by exact column-fingerprint subset, never fuzzy/partial (confirmed live: an export missing even one expected Epic column falls through to needs_mapping rather than being forced through), and both vendors' distinct column layouts reconcile onto the same four standard metric names with identical values for the same underlying data (confirmed live). Column layouts for both vendors are illustrative -- no real Epic/Cerner export sample was available to build against, unlike hcris_import.py's worksheet citations which were all confirmed against a real downloaded file; a real vendor's mapping module would need a real sample to write against. Idempotency: export_conversions keyed on a SHA-256 of the raw file bytes (not the filename -- a re-uploaded file with a new name is still the same file, a corrected file with the same name is not), confirmed live that reprocessing identical content under a different filename returns the first run's outcome without a second audit row; hospital_monthly_metrics upserts on (provider_ccn, month, metric_name). Both new tables get RLS enabled with ZERO policies, deliberately -- this is a management company's private data, not public CMS data like hospitals/cost_report_years, and no per-company scoping exists yet (STORY-006, not started), so this fails closed rather than defaulting to the public-read policy the CMS tables use. Found mid-task that the whole-project PHI guardrail (REQ-009, STORY-010) applies to this ingestion path too and wasn't being called -- the same lesson this repo already learned once for STORY-011's own grounding_guardrail sitting unticked until something called it. Wired in phi_guardrail.ingest_file_with_phi_gate() rather than rebuilding detection: confirmed live that a hospital export carrying a 'Patient Name' column is rejected (PhiRejectedError, raised rather than folded into ConversionOutcome.status so a caller can't mistake a security rejection for a normal outcome) before either export_conversions or hospital_monthly_metrics is touched, with a structured stdout audit line containing the flagged column/category/reason but never the cell value itself; a clean file re-verified working end to end afterward. Extracted the previously-duplicated load_env() into pipeline/env.py once this third file needed it, per this project's own 'three is the threshold' composition rule -- hcris_import.py and early_warning.py now import it instead of each defining their own copy; full 76-test suite re-verified green after the refactor. All live verification runs cleaned their test rows from the production tables afterward.

tests_added: pipeline/test_slipping_detector.py (12 tests: each of the 3 criteria genuinely triggering off real month-over-month values, a fully healthy hospital correctly not_slipping, no monthly data and a single month both correctly not_assessable rather than a guessed verdict, a missing value in either month not_assessable rather than a false pass, a real trigger winning over an unrelated missing metric, a gap between the two latest months correctly not_assessable rather than comparing across it, consecutive months spanning a year boundary correctly assessable, only the two latest months of a longer history being compared, and no change between months correctly not_triggered rather than not_slipping by omission)
stories.notes: REQ-016 ("surface a slipping hospital at least 4 weeks earlier than the operator's current reporting cycle") names no timestamped 'operator reporting cycle' anywhere in this system to literally measure elapsed time against. Confirmed with the user before building: the defensible reading is structural, not a literal duration -- detection runs automatically the moment a month's export is normalized (STORY-011), rather than waiting for an operator's own roughly-monthly manual review, which is what '4 weeks earlier' means in practice. Verified live: as soon as an August export was normalized, the hospital was flagged 'slipping' in the same run, with no separate review step in between. REQ-016 also gives no numeric thresholds, unlike REQ-004/REQ-005's explicit 'below 0%' / 'below 30 days' -- also confirmed with the user before building rather than inventing an unstated magic number: each of the 3 criteria (cash_on_hand declining, denial_rate_pct rising, ar_balance rising) triggers on a plain month-over-month directional change between the two latest consecutive months, mirroring STORY-004's own 'two in a row' shape for its annual AR-trend criterion but requiring only 2 months instead of 3 years since monthly data updates much faster. Same missing-data philosophy as STORY-004: a criterion with a null required metric, or whose two latest months are not genuinely consecutive calendar months (a gap, not just 'the two most recent rows'), is not_assessable, never a guessed verdict; precedence is slipping > not_assessable > not_slipping so a real trigger is never hidden behind an unrelated gap (verified: a missing cash_on_hand value alongside a genuine denial-rate spike still flags). slipping_hospital_alerts gets RLS enabled with ZERO policies, deliberately different from early_warning_flags' public-read policy -- this table is derived from hospital_monthly_metrics (STORY-011's private, operator-uploaded data), not public CMS data, and no per-company scoping exists yet (STORY-006, not started). One current-state row per hospital, replaced via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on each run, same as early_warning_flags -- confirmed live idempotent (re-running immediately after produced the same single row, not a duplicate). Verified live end to end through the real STORY-011 pipeline, not synthetic rows inserted directly: normalized two real consecutive months' exports for one hospital (cash dropping $200k to $150k, denial rate rising 5% to 9%, AR balance unchanged), then ran the detector and confirmed it correctly flagged 'slipping' with cash_on_hand_declining and denial_rate_rising both triggered (exact before/after values stored) and ar_balance_rising correctly not_triggered (unchanged is not a false positive). All live test rows deleted from the production tables afterward.
